guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 7 April 2009 sets out the terms in a section headed "Loan/credit conditions and covenants" and repeats them in its data sheet. There was no condition of loan effectiveness: the document states "Loan Effectiveness Condition: There is no loan effectiveness condition." Three covenants went into the Project Agreement. One carried a date: for the Ethnic Minority Cultural Heritage Protection component, Guizhou "shall cause a Community Project Management Group and a Village Supervision Group to be established at each of the selected minority villages by September 15, 2009, with terms of reference, staffing and other resources acceptable to the Bank", as set out in the Operation Manual for Community Participation. The second required Guizhou to carry out the project in accordance with that manual, to send the Bank any proposed amendment to it for prior approval, and to put into effect only amendments agreed with the Bank. The third required Guizhou to cause the project participants to implement Guidance No. 30 of 2007, issued by the Guizhou Provincial Party Commission and the provincial government on 28 November 2007, on safeguarding the interests of ethnic minorities and their cultural heritage in the development of rural tourism and ensuring that ethnic minorities receive the benefits of it. On money, the appraisal document states that "No specific financial management covenants are applicable to the project except for those standard financial covenants such as project audit and interim financial reports". No covenant about land acquisition or resettlement appears among the three. The consolidated Resettlement Action Plan and the Resettlement Policy Framework were prepared for the project under the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy, so the rule the renovation at Huangping Jiuzhou broke was a rule of the project's own framework, not one of the covenants the appraisal document prints.
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P091950, 7 April 2009: section III.F "Loan/credit conditions and covenants", paragraphs 47-50, repeated verbatim in the data sheet under "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any". Financial covenant sentence: Annex 7 (financial management), paragraph 34. Consolidated RAP and RPF: paragraph 64. The Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004154 of 18 December 2017 prints no covenant-compliance table; its footnote 7 and paragraph on the Huangping Jiuzhou renovation place the temporary-resettlement requirement in the RPF. Checked on this round against the document: both the prose section and the data sheet carry the same three covenants and the no-effectiveness-condition line word for word. `safeguard` rests on the covenant requiring the project participants to implement Guizhou Guidance No. 30 of 2007, not on the RAP or RPF, which no covenant requires.

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 14 April 2011 sets the terms out in a section headed "Loan/credit conditions and covenants" and repeats them in its data sheet. Money for the first disbursement category, which covers the civil works, goods, consultant services and training, could not be drawn until three things were done: the Subsidiary Agreement had been executed on behalf of the Kunming Municipal Government and the Kunming Rail Transit Company; that agreement had been duly authorised or ratified and was legally binding on both of them; and the company "has secured the land required for metro - public transport - bicycle integration according to the Integration Plan, in form and substance acceptable to the Bank". The implementation covenants required the company to prepare and send the Bank, by 15 February each year from 2012, a proposed action plan for that year's works, with the scope and schedule of activities, the financing plan and detailed budget arrangements including counterpart funds validated by the city, for the Bank's review and approval; then to carry out the works in accordance with the plan the Bank had approved; and to get the Bank's prior concurrence for any change to or waiver of the plan. Separate reporting requirements obliged the company to send the Bank half-yearly reports on implementation of the Environmental Management Plan and the Resettlement Action Plan, semi-annual progress reports by 15 February and 15 August each year from August 2011, and a mid-term review report by 31 December 2012. On money, the appraisal document states that "No specific financial covenants are applicable to the project except for standard financial covenants, e.g., project audit and interim financial reports". The Resettlement Action Plan appears in the reporting requirements; no covenant in the section requires it to be carried out.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P117656, 14 April 2011: section III.E "Loan/credit conditions and covenants", disbursement conditions and implementation covenants (a)-(c), repeated verbatim in the data sheet under "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any". Reporting requirements: section III.F, paragraph 40. Financial covenant sentence: Annex 7, paragraph 27. `land` is tagged for the disbursement condition requiring land for the integration works to be secured before the works category could be drawn on. Checked on this round against the document: the disbursement conditions, the three implementation covenants and the financial-covenant sentence all read word for word as quoted. `safeguard` rests only on the required half-yearly reports on implementation of the Environmental Management Plan and the Resettlement Action Plan, which the document prints in its reporting section and not among the covenants; the entry says so.

hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 23 April 2012 prints the terms as a table of nine "Legal Covenants" in its data sheet, each recurrent and yearly, binding each of the three provincial implementing entities. Three are about land and people. Each entity "shall, apply and caused to be applied the measures and actions set forth in its RAP in a timely and efficient manner satisfactory to the Bank" - its Resettlement Action Plan. Each "shall carry out measures for improving the living standard of Displaced Persons affected by the Project, and include provisions into the implementing contracts entered into for the implementation of the project" to ensure the environmental codes of practice and the environmental management plan were met. And no entity may "amend, suspend, fail to enforce or waive the applicable RAP, ECOP, PMP, EMP, EMDP or any annual implementation plan without the prior written approval of Bank". A fourth required each entity to "engage and retain the services of independent consultants to carry out external monitoring and reporting, and implement the recommended measures" - the third-party monitoring the completion report's demolition figures come from. The rest are administrative: maintain a provincial project leading or coordinating group, a provincial project management office and a county project management office; carry out the works in accordance with the Project Implementation Plan and the Project Agreement; implement the environmental codes of practice and pest management plan, with Gansu also implementing its ethnic minority development plan and Hunan its environmental management plan; send the Bank an annual implementation plan by 31 December each year from 2012; and apply the Financial Management Manual. The completion report records that the interim financial reports were submitted late and so "not in compliance with financial covenants in legal documents", and that procurement was carried out in accordance with the legal covenants.
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P118597, 23 April 2012: data-sheet table "Legal Covenants", all nine entries (Project Implementation Arrangement; Project Implementation Plan; Safeguards Framework-RAP; Safeguards Framework-ECOP and PMP; Process Framework; Monitoring and Reporting; Implementation; Annual Implementation Plan; Financial Management Manual), checked word for word against the document. The document prints no "Conditions" table, so no condition of effectiveness or disbursement is recorded. `safeguard` rests on the RAP, ECOP/PMP/EMDP/EMP, Process Framework and no-waiver covenants; `admin` on the leading group, management offices, implementation plan, annual plan, external monitoring and financial management manual covenants. Compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004709, 24 September 2019, paragraphs 102 and 103. `fincov` removed on check: the only money covenants here are the standard audit and interim financial report covenants and a requirement to apply the Financial Management Manual, which is a planning covenant, not a rate of return, an offtake, a use-of-proceeds limit or a required balance.

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 10 May 2012 prints the terms as a table of six "Legal Covenants" in its data sheet, and its separate "Conditions" table has a single row reading "Not applicable". One of the six covenants had to be met before money moved: before the first disbursement to a project county, the World Bank loan proceeds had to be on-lent to it "on terms and conditions satisfactory to the World Bank". The borrower also had to "Ensure adequate funding for counterpart requirements", a recurrent yearly covenant. The other four are administrative: maintain the project management and implementation units throughout implementation with qualified and adequate staff; submit the annual work plan to the Bank for its no objection by 15 December each year; conduct a mid-term review by 31 August 2015; and complete a Project Operational Manual cleared by the Bank by 30 August 2012. None of the six names land acquisition or resettlement. Resettlement action plans for the Wanzhou and Wushan sites were prepared, submitted to the Bank on 19 January 2012 and found acceptable, but the covenant table does not require them to be carried out. The documents are explicit about the limits of what the loan obliged anyone to do after the landslide. The completion report's post-closing annex states that the emergency preparedness and response plan "was not prepared for the World Bank-financed project, and the World Bank's role is limited to the provision of technical support in the review process as part of a 'no regrets' risk management contribution by the World Bank". Of the further livelihood support the Bank's mission discussed for the resettled household, the same annex says it "is not part of the RAP entitlement matrix. Rather, this is a 'beyond compliance' suggestion".
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P126210, 10 May 2012: data-sheet tables "Legal Covenants" (six entries: Project Management and Implementation Units; Counterpart Funds; On-lending agreements; Annual Review of Work plan; Mid-Term Review; Project Operational Manual) and "Conditions" (single row reading "Not applicable"), checked word for word. RAPs prepared and accepted: section IV.E, paragraph 55. The two quotations on what was not required: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005207, 29 October 2021, Annex 6 "Post-Closing Report for the Outstanding Environmental and Social Issues", paragraph 3 (EPRP) and paragraph 10 (beyond-compliance suggestion). The absence of a resettlement covenant rests on the data-sheet covenant table being the appraisal document's own complete list of the loan's legal covenants. Two corrections on check: the completion report is ICR00005207, not ICR00004869; and the claim that "no condition of effectiveness or of disbursement was attached" was cut, because the on-lending covenant is itself a thing to be done before first disbursement to a county. `fincov` removed: on-lending on acceptable terms and counterpart funding are neither a rate of return, an offtake, a use-of-proceeds limit nor a required balance.

xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 20 May 2013 prints the terms as a table of two "Legal Covenants" and one "Condition" in its data sheet. The condition was one of effectiveness: the loan could not become effective until Xuancheng Municipality, through the development zone, entered into a Subsidiary Agreement with the zone's construction and investment company. The first covenant carried the date 30 June 2014: the company "shall have entered into a contract for the construction, and at least 5 years of operation and maintenance, of the wastewater treatment plant of the Project, with an entity or entities duly qualified to perform such tasks, all under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank", cited to Section IV.A.1 of the schedule to the Project Agreement. The second is a cost-recovery covenant, recurrent and yearly: "For each of the Borrower's fiscal years starting 2018, the Wastewater Treatment Plant, should have total revenues equivalent to not less than its total operating expenses, excluding depreciation", cited to Section IV.A.2. The completion report states that "All the legal covenants were complied with on time." Neither covenant names land acquisition, house demolition or resettlement. The resettlement action plan of April 2013 and a Resettlement Policy Framework were prepared, the framework because the sites of the later land sales to industry were not yet known. For plots sold after the loan's closing date, the appraisal document records not a requirement but a promise: "the client has agreed that any land acquisition and resettlement activities will be undertaken in a manner consistent with the provisions set out in the RPF".
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P129431, 20 May 2013: data-sheet tables "Legal Covenants" (two entries, citing Project Agreement Schedule Section IV, A.1 and A.2) and "Conditions" (one entry, type Effectiveness, Subsidiary Agreement), checked word for word. RAP and RPF, and the "client has agreed" sentence: section IV.F, paragraphs 63-65, repeated in Annex 3. Compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005221, 23 February 2021, paragraph 97. The absence of a resettlement covenant rests on the data-sheet covenant table being the appraisal document's own complete list. `fincov` is carried by the cost-recovery covenant, a required self-financing ratio. `admin` removed on check: neither the Subsidiary Agreement condition nor the plant construction and operation contract sets up an agency, a plan or a committee.

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.conditions_add: The emergency project paper of 22 January 2009 sets the terms out in a section headed "Terms and conditions for project financing", which says that "In addition to the standard covenants relating to implementation arrangements, reporting, fiduciary requirements, etc., the following specific conditions are included in the loan agreements". Its data sheet answers the printed question "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any" with the word "None", and then lists the same conditions under it stage by stage. Nothing was required before negotiation, Board presentation or effectiveness: both lines read "None". Four things had to be done before money could be drawn: payment of the front-end fee; adoption by Sichuan and Gansu provinces of the Operations Manual, including the Environmental and Social Screening and Assessment Framework and the Financial Management Manual; approval of sub-projects by the Bank and by government; and adoption of the Procurement Plan by the two provinces. Because the sub-projects were not chosen when the loan was approved, that framework is where the obligations on land and people sit. The implementation covenants required the provinces to maintain the provincial project leading groups, the project management offices and the local project implementing units throughout the project; to "apply the OM, the ESSAF and the FMM in carrying out the project"; to ensure sub-projects met the agreed eligibility criteria and were prepared taking the Bank's comments into account, and, where the Bank's prior review was required, to implement them only after the Bank had approved them; to "implement sub-projects in accordance with implementation plans to be prepared, and plans to mitigate any adverse environmental and social impacts to be prepared pursuant to the ESSAF"; and to carry out capacity building and technical assistance in accordance with proposals approved by the Bank. The framework itself, the document says, sets procedures for identifying eligible project-affected people, determining compensation, exploring and implementing rehabilitation measures, and management and monitoring. That last covenant is the one the Moba Gorge forest-land payment of 650 yuan per mu fell short of: the plan the Bank had approved set 1,744 to 3,160 yuan per mu, and the completion report says the compensation "was below agreed rates".
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.why: World Bank Emergency Project Paper, P114107, 22 January 2009: section G "Terms and conditions for project financing", paragraph 105 (the conditions for negotiation, effectiveness and disbursement and the five implementation covenants (a)-(e)), repeated in the data sheet on page 6; Annex 7, paragraph 12, repeats three of the four disbursement conditions. What the ESSAF covers for resettlement: section IV.F, paragraph 86. Non-compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003783, 27 February 2017, paragraph 49 ("below agreed rates and is being rectified by GPG") and Annex 6, which gives the approved rates of RMB 3,160 and RMB 1,744 per mu against RMB 650 per mu actually paid. The data-sheet page was rasterised on check: "None" sits on the same line as the printed question, so it answers that question rather than heading the four stage lines below it; either way it does not displace paragraph 105, which states in the body of the document that the disbursement conditions are in the loan agreements.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.conditions_add: The Zhamushui works were not in the loan when it was approved. They were added as a fifth component in July 2006 by an amendment to the Loan Agreement, with a Project Agreement for the Guangrun company dated 4 January 2007, and that Project Agreement is not published. What the published documents do show is that the loan's own instruments were widened to cover the new works: a later amendment letter of 11 January 2012, signed by the Ministry of Finance, Hubei province and the company, restates the Loan Agreement's definitions so that the Guangrun company is one of the "Project Companies", the Zhamushui and Hongwawu works are "Part E" of the project, and the "Resettlement Action Plans" of the loan include "the resettlement action plan, acceptable to the Bank, dated December 7, 2005 ... for the compensation, resettlement and rehabilitation of Affected Persons in respect of Part E of the Project". The same letter records that the company's obligations under the January 2007 Project Agreement were assumed by its successor and that all other terms of both agreements "shall remain in full force and effect", without printing them. For the four original components the appraisal document of 30 May 2002 does print the terms. Execution of the subsidiary loan agreements between the government and Hubei, and between Hubei and the project companies through their prefecture and county governments, was a condition of loan effectiveness. Bank approval of the environmental management plans for the transmission lines was a condition of disbursement for the matching expenditure categories. Hubei had to maintain a project management office with terms of reference and resources satisfactory to the Bank, and to on-lend the loan to the project companies on the same terms as the Bank loan, with the companies carrying the foreign exchange risk. On land and people, Hubei had to "cause each of the project counties to enter into arrangements satisfactory to the Bank with the project company located in such county" for the resettlement, compensation and rehabilitation of all persons affected by its part of the project "in accordance with the respective RAPs and RPFs", and each project company had to carry out its part of the project in accordance with its own plan. Each of those project counties had to set up a poverty alleviation enhancement fund and put into it 20 per cent of the fiscal revenues the project brought the county, for at least five years after operations began, and before commissioning its first generating unit each of those project companies had to open a debt service reserve account and pay all net revenues into it until it held the next six months' principal and interest. Those 2002 covenants name the four original project companies and counties, and the terms written for the Guangrun company in January 2007 are not published, so what they said cannot be read off them. The completion report does record that under the Project Agreement 20 per cent of the county's fiscal revenue from the project went to the county poverty alleviation fund, and that Guangrun's five-year contribution to the Jianshi County fund was to start in June 2012, after the Zhamushui plant was commissioned.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, China - Hubei Hydroelectric Development in Poor Areas Project (P068049, Loan 4666-CHA), 30 May 2002, section G "Main Loan Conditions": the effectiveness condition; agreements reached with Hubei province (project management office; on-lending with foreign exchange risk; involuntary resettlement arrangements in accordance with the RAPs and RPFs; environment; the 20 per cent fiscal-revenue poverty fund); agreements reached with the project companies (carry out its respective part in accordance with its respective RAP and RPF; debt service reserve account). Disbursement condition on transmission-line EMPs: Annex 6, paragraph 4. Phase evidence, added on check and fetched in this round: World Bank, "Amendments to the Loan Agreement and Project Agreement for Loan 4666-CN", letter of 11 January 2012, saved as /home/claude/r22/cache/P068049_AMEND2012.pdf and .txt - amendments A.1, A.3, A.4, A.5(aa), A.6(ll), A.7 and section B, and the closing "remain in full force and effect" sentence. Also fetched: the restructuring project paper of 17 January 2011 (P068049_RESTR2011) and its data sheet, which record the July 2006 loan amendment adding Guangrun and say the fifth component comprised Bank-financed equipment with counterpart-funded civil works. July 2006 amendment and 4 January 2007 Project Agreement: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR0000339, 14 June 2012, paragraph 16 and Annex 12, item 3; poverty fund including Guangrun: the same report, Annex 10, paragraphs 3-5. `fincov` is carried by the debt service reserve account, a required minimum balance, scoped in the prose to the four original project companies. Excluded under the ordinary-commercial-terms rule: the 1.2 debt service ratio, the 80:20 debt-to-equity limit, the 20 per cent working-expenses-to-revenues ratio, the dividend restriction, the 30-year maturity, 5-year grace and 0.25 per cent front-end fee.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.conditions_add: The terms are in the Project Agreement for Loan 4727, the conformed copy dated 12 May 2004, whose Schedule 2 binds the city of Wuhan. In carrying out the road network and public transport parts, Wuhan had to "take, or cause to be taken, all necessary actions to minimize to the extent possible any involuntary loss by persons of shelter, productive assets or access to productive assets or of income or means of livelihood", to "carry out the EMPs, RAPs and the RPF, in a manner satisfactory to the Bank", and to send the Bank for prior approval any proposed revision to them. Before starting work on any activity not in those plans that needed land, Wuhan had to "prepare a resettlement action plan satisfactory to the Bank, in accordance with the principles and procedures set forth in the Resettlement Policy Framework" and send it to the Bank for approval, and to do the same for an environmental assessment and management plan. A resettlement plan for the Sanjintan to Ping'anpu section of the Middle Ring was prepared on 1 July 2007, three years after the loan was appraised; it describes itself as a sub-project of the Bank-financed project whose resettlement is to follow the plan the Bank approved. Wuhan also could not change the agreed road activities unless the change was compatible with the Wuhan Urban Transport Strategy and a full feasibility study acceptable to the Bank had been carried out. It had to maintain until the project was finished the Municipal Project Leading Group, chaired by the mayor or a deputy mayor, and the Project Office, headed by a qualified manager and with units responsible for land acquisition and resettlement, environmental management, procurement, financial management, construction management, project management and monitoring and reporting, each headed by a manager acceptable to the Bank; to keep a team of construction supervision experts in place until completion; and by 30 November each year from 2004 to send the Bank a proposed annual work programme and budget and then implement what was agreed. The Loan Agreement's financial covenants are the standard ones: keep a financial management system, have the accounts audited each year by independent auditors acceptable to the Bank, and furnish the audited statements within six months. Whether these obligations were met cannot be checked here: no completion report for this project is published, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it prints no covenant-compliance table. The review does relay from the unpublished completion report that the project was in compliance with the Bank's environmental and social safeguard policies, and that the resettlement cost almost twice what was estimated at appraisal and was paid for entirely by the borrower.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.why: World Bank, Conformed Copy - L4727 - Wuhan Urban Transport Project - Project Agreement, 12 May 2004, Schedule 2, paragraphs 1 (Municipal Project Leading Group), 2 (Project Office and its units), 3 (Project Implementation Plan and annual work programme), 4 (construction supervision team), 5 (minimise involuntary loss; carry out the EMPs, RAPs and RPF; prior approval of revisions), 6 (new RAP under the RPF before work not in the RAPs) and 8 (no change to the agreed activities). Definitions of RAPs and RPF: Conformed Copy - L4727 - Loan Agreement, 12 May 2004, Sections 1.02(k) and (l); financial covenants: Article IV, Section 4.01. Both were fetched in this round from the World Bank documents API and saved as /home/claude/r22/cache/P069852_PA_L4727.pdf and P069852_LA_L4727.pdf with their .txt conversions. The same obligations are summarised in the Project Appraisal Document, Report No. 25590, 12 February 2004, section G "Main Loan Conditions", G.2.3.1 and G.2.3.2. Sanjintan - Ping'anpu plan: Resettlement Action Plan RP603, 1 July 2007, section 3, fetched in this round and saved as P069852_RAP_RP603.pdf. No compliance record: Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13574, 27 June 2011, which carries no covenant-compliance table; its safeguards and costs paragraphs are the source of the last sentence. A search of the documents API for the completion report itself returned none.
